title: ARDUINO-MQTT/135
body: Hello Joel, just to let you know: I recently upgraded the esp8266 board library to 2.5.0-beta2 Your library works for normal connections, but not for TLS using WiFiClientSecure, if the above mentioned board library is installed. In the log of my mosquitto broker (on Raspberry Pi) I see, that the device is trying to connect: `New connection from 192.168.11.84 on port 8883` On the device side, client.connect() never becomes true. I tried to ignore this test and submitted a payload to a topic on the broker, it never arrived there. It seems safe to assume, that the connection somehow is not correctly working I downgraded to 2.4.2, everything is back to normal and working flawlessly. From what I read on the github page of the ESP8266 project, they did a lot of work under the hood. Probably it is best to wait a few days or even weeks before digging into this, but this is up to you.

title: OCTOPRINT-ASTROPRINT/26
body: I just had a user report an odd issue in foosel/OctoPrint#2442. They have the Astroprint plugin disabled, and that makes them not able to login anymore. A closer look at OctoPrint's plugin subsystem reveals that contrary to what I so far assumed, plugins are still loaded even when disabled. Which means that in your case the plugin's implementation will be initialized, and in its constructor functions will be attached to Flask Login's loggedIn and loggedOut signals that try to send messages to the frontend via `self._plugin_manager` - however, if your plugin is disabled, your plugin won't be fully initialized, `self._plugin_manager` hence not injected and that means things crash inside Flask Login when trying to call your signal handler and the login fails with an HTTP 500. I'll have to do something about this on OctoPrint's side, however I strongly suggest to not attach any stuff to the system as long as the plugin is not fully initialized (read: the `initialized` method on it is called). Could you fix this on your end? As I said, I'll also look into finding a good fix on mine. If push comes to shove, disabled plugins will simply get the same treatment that blacklisted ones get, meaning some metadata will be missing in the plugin list but no code will be executed at all, preventing such issues in the future.

Are you aware that the IoTHubClient has a feature called Retry Policy? The default retry policy is EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF_WITH_JITTER. It means that if there is a disconnection, the client will retry connecting within 1 second, then 2 secs, 4, 8, ... eventually taking a long time (hours) if the connection has been disrupted for too long. 
The exponential retry policy is not recommended for connections that stay offline for too long (several minutes). 

You can control the retry policy by using this [API function](https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-c/blob/master/iothub_client/inc/iothub_client_ll.h#L375).

title: AZURE-IOT-SDK-C/688
body: Initially opened on https://github.com/Azure/azure-iot-sdk-python/issues/216 If MQTT is unable to establish a connection, it will keep trying and once it succeeds queued messages will be sent to the Cloud. However, if for some reason we can't get past the initial connection phase, then SDK does not respect message timeouts. An easy way to repro this is to just send a few messages with networking enabled via convenience sample, then disable your network in middle. What is happening is that in `IoTHubTransport_MQTT_Common_DoWork`, we have logic that will compare max # of retries and ultimately call `sendMsgComplete(mqttMsgEntry->iotHubMessageEntry, transport_data, IOTHUB_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT);` which tells caller that we should timeout. However - if the initial call to `InitializeConnection` at the top of this function fails, then we never get into the correct spot in the loop to check the timeouts. Note there is at IoTHub_Client layer a `DoTimeouts` API. However it doesn't save us here because its already transferred the messages from its pending queue to MQTT's waitingForAck. To fix this A) Checking for message timeouts should not be conditional on state of MQTT itself. And B) It feels more natural to be the timeout based on actual timing, instead of checking whether a retry has occurred or not. C) The code in the block `Codes_SRS_IOTHUB_TRANSPORT_MQTT_COMMON_07_057` also needs review. After we timeout the 1st timed out message, it looks like we unconditionally run through the queued messages and reset their retryCount=0. If we just did (B) though, this would be moot.

body: - **OS and version used:** Linux - **SDK version used:** release_2018_10_03 # Description of the issue: The problem to be solved is that the attempt to connect to Azure sometimes fails at the low level, and the low level debug messages make this plain, but nothing is communicated back to the high level functions that we are using. Examples would be an unauthorized ConnectionString or bad proxy settings. Without this, much time passes until you find that you can’t send messages; that is your clue that the connection was not opened. The callback for the Connection Status change is not being invoked here, presumably because it has not yet *changed*. Looking at the existing Azure APIs, none is quite right for getting at this. Adding a getter for the Connection Status would be one option, though that may be a fair amount of work since the mocking function must also be provided, and tests to validate it. What I chose to do was to patch the closest of the existing APIs, GetSendStatus. Normally this returns IOTHUB_CLIENT_OK if it is able to get the SendStatus (which is either Idle or Busy, returned as an output parameter). My simple patch was to return IOTHUB_CLIENT_ERROR from the low level IoTHubTransport_AMQP_Common_GetSendStatus() function if transport’s state is not Connected or Connecting. I think a better choice, if still using the same API signature for GetSendStatus, would be to extend the set of enums from just Idle and Busy to add NotConnected or somesuch. The justification for leaning on this API could be that NotConnected is an indication of "why you can’t Send right now". # Code sample exhibiting the issue: My patch, for AMQP over websockets, is provided here. I recommend adding the new enum instead of what I did, but the patch shows the way. I think MQTT will have a similar solution. The pause between each try increases as expected. - I update the device twin desired properties using Device Explorer. - Hitting refresh shows the new values as expected. - I plug-in the network cable again. - The client SDK output shows that it regained connectivity. - I wait a few seconds, and it successfully gets the entire device twin again. Now, at this point, I expect to get the updates I made in #3 – however, I get the old version. Moreover, if I look at the desired properties using Device Explorer, I see my changes from #3 got reverted. The version stamp remains the same – but the values are the old one.

body: Hi team, thank you for great work and quick response! I saw segmentation fault (or access violation in Windows) from `Gateway_CreateFromJson`. The debugger said that the exception had been thrown from jvm.dll which had been called https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c# ### Environment * Windows 10 x64 with CU * Using NuGet package (https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Azure.Devices.Gateway.Native.Windows.x64/) * I manually extracted the dll and pdb from the package's `runtime` folder to investigate. * Oracle JDK 8u 131 ### Additional information: * My code calls `Broker#publish()` and wait for "response message" for request-response style messaging for initialization in `GatewayModule#start()`. * When I commented out `Broker#publish()` call from `GatewayModule#start()`, the segfault looked disappear. * As of our logging code in Java, `GatewayModule#start()` finished successfully. * Another module sent messages to the Java module continuously. * The debugger said that the invalid address is almost '0x270' and '0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` once. * I failed to check call stack when I saw '0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`. ### Hypothesis As far as I look, I found similar error in [Xamarin Android](https://bugzilla.xamarin.com/show_bug.cgi?id=13521#c17), it is race condition of `JNIEnv*`. So, my hypothesis of this issue is race condition of `env` field of `MODULE_JAVA_DATA` as following: 1. The java host module initializes `JAVA_MODULE_HANDLE_DATA` as module data in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L116). 2. The `module_worker` created from the broker, passing `module_info` in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/core/src/broker.c#L373). 3. The `JavaModuleHost_Start` calls JNI's `AttachCurrentThread` and stores `JNIEnv*` in the field of `module` argument in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L473). I will call this thread as "main-thread". 4. The `module_worker` calles `JavaModuleHost_Receive` simultaneously, and it also calls JNI's `AttachCurrentThread` and then stores `JNIEnv*` in the field of `module` argument in [this line](https://github.com/Azure/iot-edge/blob/master/bindings/java/src/java_module_host.c#L407). This step overwrites `JNIEnv*` for "main-thread". I will call this thread as "worker-thread" 5. The `GatewayModule#start()` is finished, then ``JavaModuleHost_Start` calls JNI's `ExceptionOccurred` with overwritten. It causes segmentation fault. * If the "worker-thread" already called `DetachCurrentThread`, it is reasonable the `env` field was invalidated with jvm as `-1L`. So I think that `JNIEnv*` should be stored in the local variable instead of "effectively global" variable in the struct, ant it may solve this problem. In fact, it just works in our testing environment. Any idea? Thank you for always.

comments:
[2018-07-10T20:24:57Z | RobertLucian | comment]
The values which were getting overwritten on other readings was caused by bad timing on the GrovePi and a lack of organizing the requests one after the another in an orderly manner. 

A mechanism to check if there's available data on the GrovePi has been added which basically reduces the need to use `sleep`s on the Pi. Now, we can just poll the GrovePi until it gets a response for the requested data. 

Huge improvements to the sample rate on basic functions (reading/writing on digital/analog ports, ultrasonic sensor, etc) have been brought. Before these improvements, in order to have a reliable connection to the GrovePi and still be able to poll the GrovePi for values (or for writing to ports) a sample rate of 10-15 was doable - now we can see sample rates of up to 380 while the system is running without any hiccups.

The DHT sensor at the moment takes roughly 550 ms for a reading. I think that number can be brought down to a half. It still needs to be investigated.

[2018-07-11T12:03:24Z | RobertLucian | comment]
The firmware would resort to reading twice for both the temperature and humidity sensor (with the DHT11) and that was quite inefficient. I have come up with another function in the firmware that does both of them in one run, thus taking the reading time down to ~280ms (up to 3.54 samples / sec from ~1.7 samples / sec).

[2018-07-11T18:12:28Z | RobertLucian | comment]
Support for the IR receiver has been added. What's super confusing is that there was a IR-related function in `grovepi.py` but it didn't do anything. The same thing for the firmware. 

So, long story short, we now also have support for the IR receiver on the GrovePi. I'm getting 150-170 samples / sec for the IR receiver, which to me I'd say it's a success.

Thanks for the report. This looks like it's the exact same problem as in #411. I'm already debugging it and I'm trying to see where this comes from.

@yeeking in the first case, were NaNs the only thing you were seeing? If not, have you considered reading the DHT sensor until you'd get valid data and then repeat the process?

title: NEEO-SDK/23
body: From express/server.js - you set the routes like '/db' - routeDatabase '/device' - routeDevice '/' - routeDeviceRegistration '/db/search' for device search '/db/{0}' where device definition '/device/xxx' - device discovery/set/get values '/xxx' - adapter subscription The problem really occurs with the last one - where 'xxx' is defined as '/:adapterName/yyy' What if I was very bad and decided to name my adapter "db" or "device"?!? Routing would get really screwed up since I was able to match a different route. Same goes if you change the device ID to a string - then I could have a device id of "search" and screw that part up. The routes should be more explicit - something like '/db/search' '/db/get' '/device/discovery/xxx' '/device/get/xxx' '/device/set/xxx' '/device/subscribe/xxx' '/device/unsubscribe/xxx' That way they 'dynamic' part of the route can't screw up your routing.

After=network-online.target

body: Discovered this issue when working on a separate project that depends on TuyAPI. (I believe this may be the root cause of https://github.com/codetheweb/tuyapi/issues/158 and https://github.com/codetheweb/tuyapi/issues/103.) I added a condition to the data event handler for the socket that checks if the parsed and returned data is an object; if not it would throw an error. After adding this, tests started failing. I discovered that on a fast enough machine (and testing against a local stub) it's possible to overwrite data sent to the socket by calling `.set()` and/or `.get()` quickly after each other. Data has already been being overwritten in the test suite, but it wasn't caught because I didn't add a check to see if the returned data was an object or not. For instance, running the test suite generated this beautiful packet: ```  ``` ~~Obviously invalid~~. title: TUYA-CONVERT/187
body: Hi, When launching start_flash.sh on Lubuntu 18.04, I have an error in the log file : Dnsmasq cannot strat because address is already in use. And effectively, the port 53 is already used by systemd-resolved. To solve this problem, I had to edit scripts/setup.asp and add the following line to /etc/dnsmasq.conf, juste after interface=$WLAN 👍 bind-interfaces listen-address=10.42.42.1 This allowes Dnsmasq to start on a different IP than systemd-resolved. body: ## Description It's possible that I'm misunderstanding the expected behavior, but I'm not sure the overrides are behaving properly. ## Configuration ```yaml entity_controller: closet: sensor: binary_sensor.0x00158d0003cc4255_occupancy entity: light.shelly1_2c76fa_relay_0 sensor_type: duration delay: 30 overrides: - sensor.foo ``` ## Steps to reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Trigger motion sensor (light turns on) 2. Set override state (`sensor.foo`) to on ### Expected behavior EC stops changing the state; the light that was on remains on forever. (if the motion sensor was not triggered before `sensor.off` went from `off` to `on`, the light should stay off forever) ### Actual Behaviour EC immediately shuts off the light (if the motion sensor was not triggered before `sensor.off` went from `off` to `on`, the light does in fact stay off forever) ## Logs ``` 2019-12-14 22:12:50 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.entity_controller.closet] <state light.shelly1_2c76fa_relay_0=off; friendly_name=Closet Light, supported_features=0 @ 2019-12-14T22:12:33.846364+02:00> 2019-12-14 22:12:50 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Exited state idle 2019-12-14 22:12:50 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.entity_controller.closet] {'delay': 30, 'service_data': None, 'service_data_off': None} 2019-12-14 22:12:50 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Entered state active_timer 2019-12-14 22:12:50 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Entered state active 2019-12-14 22:12:50 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.entity_controller.closet] <state light.shelly1_2c76fa_relay_0=on; friendly_name=Closet Light, supported_features=0 @ 2019-12-14T22:12:50.067048+02:00> 2019-12-14 22:12:59 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Exited state active_timer 2019-12-14 22:12:59 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Exited state active 2019-12-14 22:12:59 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Entered state overridden 2019-12-14 22:12:59 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Exited state idle 2019-12-14 22:12:59 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Entered state overridden 2019-12-14 22:13:01 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Exited state overridden 2019-12-14 22:13:01 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Entered state idle 2019-12-14 22:13:01 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Exited state overridden 2019-12-14 22:13:01 INFO (MainThread) [transitions.core] Entered state idle ``` ## Version Commit 86878f7

[2019-12-20T10:24:35Z | mikeage | comment]
ok, now that I understand the code a bit, it's clear why this happens:

```python
     def on_exit_active(self):
         self.log.debug("Turning off entities, cancelling timer")
         self._cancel_timer()  # cancel previous timer
         self.update(delay=self.lightParams.get(
             CONF_DELAY))  # no need to update immediately
         self.turn_off_control_entities()
```

It happens to be quite annoying for my personal use case, but on the other hand, if the behavior would change (and it'd require rewriting *how* the lights get shut off when leaving active), we could very easily get into blocked states when the override variable becomes `off` again.

[2019-12-20T13:01:57Z | danobot | comment]
The idea of overrides is to stop EC from activating in the first place, which works correctly as shown in GIF below. I hadn't considered this case in the original design because it is not a use case of mine.

If EC is in **active_timer**, turning on an override entity will cause EC to exit **active_timer** and enter the *overridden** state. An unintended side effect is that the control entities are turned off, which is counter intuitive.

![103](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7984567/71256141-e98c1a00-236a-11ea-8efd-777a249841b7.gif)

The definition of **active** and all its substates is that the control entites are turned on when in that state. We could add a new state called **active_overridden** as a dirty solution. This then asks for equivalent states for **blocked**. is there a cleaner way to do this? What will fulfil the requirement?
I agree that the light state should be maintained as activating an override entity means "Leave the light the way it is and ceise further interaction with it"

[2019-12-20T13:52:31Z | mikeage | comment]
Now that I understand more, I agree it works as designed; I just didn't like the design  :)

Active_overriden would probably work. Another idea might be to move the turn_off into the destination states (not, of course, including overridden). 

One caveat is that exiting overridden shouldn't go into blocked, I think. It's similar to the restart HA case, but probably more common.

[2019-12-21T19:21:23Z | mikeage | comment]
What do you think about constrained? Should a light that's on when we enter the constrained time be shut off? Does constrain mean "don't touch it any more" or "don't let the lights be on because of EC now"? I first assumed the former, but then it's really just a version of override with a built in time, so maybe you had something else in mind.

[I'm working on an implementation for the main issue here; it's actually seeming pretty straightforward, but I want to do some more testing before I share]

[2019-12-22T02:11:53Z | danobot | comment]
I guess constrained means EC is overriding itself. Override means some other entity is overriding EC. Checkt He readme, I think there's a description of each state. Seems very similar now that it think about it.

This component is about eliminating annoying things caused by dumb, basic automations. To stay true to that purpose, a light that is on when EC enters constrained should stay on. Is this easy to implement or are we completely breaking the state machine by doing this? Seems like EC state and light state are no longer congruent.

[2019-12-22T07:34:25Z | mikeage | comment]
I saw the readme, but I was trying to understand more about your motivations, beyond just what's written.

Just to be clear, I'm not proposing breaking EC (at least, I don't think I am; keep calling me out if you think I'm getting too far). What I'm trying to do is make it serve not just as a full control for lights (for which it's perfect as-is) but also as a replacement for the same automations if one wants to have lights that are usually automatic but also occasionally manually controlled. For example, in the bathroom, I always want the light to come on when I walk in. In the bedroom, I generally always want it during the hours when people are awake, but sometimes, I might want to nap in the middle of the day and so I want to tell it "ok, leave this off now". Conversely, there are times when I normally want it not to trigger, but in a few cases, I might want to say "keep this light on for now". And if/when I say "go back to pure automatic control", I don't want it to shut off and then turn back on from the motion that comes 1 second later. It's a bad experience, and it's bad for lights that are on smart relays (a smart LED couldn't care less, but a fluorescent fixture with a ballast really shouldn't be toggled like that).  But again, keep me in line if you think these are rather specific cases that don't scale out to others' applications.

[2019-12-22T09:05:49Z | danobot | comment]
We are on the same page, just coming up with a way to implement it :)
Did you see the `stay` option? theres a special state **active_stay_on**. once in this state, EC will remain on. 
You mention a lot of different usecases (too many to focus on in this issue).

What is the proposed solution for this override issue? I agree that the light should remain on when EC enters override state. How can we achieve this?
You suggested moving the `turn_off` call to the destination state. Let's go with that for now. We then need to check each transition from **active** to determine if the light should be shut off. 

In terms of implementation you can go ahead and place the `turn_off` calls in destinatino states, but make sure they only fire when the source state was **active**. 

f your testing shows this has no weird side effects, then you can modify the **override** state such that the light remains untouched when it is entered from the **active** state. I still think this will create messy inconsistencies. theres no point discussing it, just go ahead and try it and see what happens :)

[2019-12-22T12:16:04Z | mikeage | comment]
I didn't see any documentation about `stay`, but I did see the code. Can you give me a one sentence overview?

My main use case is as follows; I have certain times of day (and certain days of the week) where I want the lights to be on even if no one is observed, and certain times when I want the lights off even if people are present. It's a bit too complicated for the `constrained` option, so I have a sensor (probably should be a binary_sensor, but whatever). Whenever I activate this sensor, I want the motion sensors to be effectively completely disconnected. 

Is there a reason not to always call `turn_off` upon entering idle? Can this cause any harm?

[2019-12-22T12:22:26Z | danobot | comment]
You will need to experiment when to call `turn_off`.
You're right `stay` is undocumented. If I remember right, adding `stay: true` to the config means that EC will enter **active** and remain in that state until the light is manually turned off.
I think this was requested in an issue, can't find it right now. Will add it to the readme.

ok, I'll experiment. Just as an FYI, I'm going to be going on vacation in a day or two... not from work, which would give me time, but from my house, which means I can't experiment. So if it takes me a while to get back, it doesn't mean I lost interest or gave up :-)

body: Azure Service Bus has the behavior that idle AMQP 1.0 links are closed after ~10 minutes of idle timeout. We get following log message and afterwards the AMQP 1.0 Azure Service Bus connection is in a strange state: ``` Consumer <org.apache.qpid.jms.JmsMessageConsumer@3b8f105d> closed due to JmsConnectionRemotelyClosedException: The connection was inactive for more than the allowed 120000 milliseconds and is closed by container '...'. [condition = amqp:connection:forced] ``` "Strange" because: after that message we get following messages: ``` May 23rd 2019, 06:56:14.973 Session closed: org.apache.qpid.jms.JmsSession@3230bc47 - Unknown error from remote peer May 23rd 2019, 06:56:14.975 Connection interrupted: amqps://<...>.servicebus.windows.net:5671?amqp.saslMechanisms=PLAIN&transport.trustAll=true&transport.verifyHost=false May 23rd 2019, 06:56:16.229 Connection restored: amqps://<...>.servicebus.windows.net:5671?amqp.saslMechanisms=PLAIN&transport.trustAll=true&transport.verifyHost=false ``` The last 2 messages repeat themselves each second. We could/should react on `org.eclipse.ditto.services.connectivity.messaging.amqp.AmqpClientActor.StatusReportingListener#onConsumerClosed` and restore the connection. What also can be seen: the default JMS client timeout seems to be 120s (see error message above) - we should increase that to at least 5 min. Azure Service Bus' timeout seems to be ~9-11 minutes. I'm not sure why this only happens on Service Bus - as for Eclipse Hono we also have consumers which are "idling" 2 minutes. Maybe the AMQP endpoint does however keep them open infinitely. @kaizimmerm : could you please have a look on this?

Hi @kaizimmerm,
I just repoduced this by creating a Service Bus instance and connecting to it using the Qpid JMS Client (the client we use in Ditto for connections to AMQP 1.0 brokers). I traced the communication between client and server, the service bus sets an idle timeout of 240000ms in the open frame. This value is interpreted by the Qpid JMS client and it would send a PING to keep the connection open after 120000ms ("remote idle timeout" / 2). Unfortunately the connection is closed after 60s by the link tracker:
> The connection was inactive for more than the allowed 60000 milliseconds and is closed by container 'LinkTracker'

So it seems that the Service Bus does not respect the idle timeout set by itself. I can provide a simple reproducer if required. title: SMARTHOME/2849
body: The values of outputs of other modules are made available to script, which is also directly supported by the rule editor: ![screen shot 2017-01-18 at 10 15 23](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3244965/22057952/507b7474-dd67-11e6-88b9-7b4b69045d65.png) When trying to access those outputs, an exception is thrown. The problem is that in the rule context, they are made available as e.g. "1.newState", which is provided as a map 1->newState in within the rule execution context. It is probably rather a bad idea to define "1" as a variable name...
comments:
[2017-01-18T16:36:08Z | danchom | comment]
The keys of outputs in rule context are in form "moduleId.outputId". Here  "1.newState" the 1 is the moduleId. If you have modules of the same module type (they will have same output uids), what "newState" will you get?

[2017-01-18T16:37:46Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
See https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/2850#issue-201521946.

[2017-01-18T16:41:51Z | danchom | comment]
ok but if you have 2 item modules
print(context.get('1.newState')) - will return the state of the first one
print(context.get('2.newState')) -  will return the state of the second one
print(newState) - what will return this? State of the first or the second item?

[2017-01-18T16:45:08Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
> what will return this?

Undefined, it might be the one or the other. That's why you should use the other option in case you have the same output id twice.

[2017-01-18T19:24:39Z | danchom | comment]
For me, the right way here, is to use inputs in script module and the script must be write using them. In that way the scripts can be reused and will not depend on state of the system (The inputs always will be available, the outputs of other modules can missed in rule context). Btw the inputs are also in available in rule context under their names.

[2017-01-18T20:32:21Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
@danchom We discussed that already a long time ago: You are mixing up users with developers here.
Only developers have a chance to define a module TYPE (on which they could declare inputs that their script needs). But the usecase at hand here is for the (expert) end user: He uses the existing "ScriptAction" and can get hold of the rule context to do fancy stuff. Note that this "user" feature has been introduced a long time ago already and the Paper UI supports offering the outputs since a few months. And imho, this is a very neat feature for the end user.

What you are talking about are rather "scripted action types" - this is something that will be addressed with https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/pull/1783. And yes, there you would clearly define inputs for your scripted type, so that you can easily match it etc. But this means that the script is part of the module type and not of the module itself.

[2017-01-19T07:23:05Z | danchom | comment]
May be I was not clear, I'm not talking about #1783. My proposal was to add some numbers of inputs (5 or 10) to the current ScriptCondition and ScriptAction module types. In that way the users will have ability  connect them to outputs of other modules (module connections are not part of the module type, they are part of rule creation and can be done by the users) and the advance users will have opportunity to write scripts using these connected inputs (the rule engine set their values and make available in the rule context).
The current approach has followin cons:
- Only the outputs of the module which was triggered are available in the rule context. For example : 
1 - is  ItemTrigger module for the first item
2 -  is  ItemTrigger module for the second item
and the first Item change its state
print(context.get('1.newState')) - will print the new state 
print(context.get('2.newState')) - won't be available in rule context. (because at the moment all the outputs are stateless)
print(context.get('newState')) - won't know state of which item is printed.
BTW I want to open discussion about stateless / stateful outputs. I know that we have discuss this but I think we can do some improvements. I'll add an issue about that, 

- this script "print(context.get('1.newState'))" can't be reused or can stop working because it relays on the module name. When the user change the name of the module, the rule will be compromised.

[2017-01-19T08:14:50Z | sjsf | comment]
> My proposal was to add some numbers of inputs (5 or 10) to the current ScriptCondition and ScriptAction module types.

Why do you think it's convenient to have a fixed number of inputs and force the user to wire them in an additional step? In the end, the user will have to "remember" what exactly "input3" was. I can really recommend trying this out yourself!

> Only the outputs of the module which was triggered are available in the rule context.

Of course, this is what I would expect. What kind of useful input should come module wich did _not_ trigger the rule?

> When the user change the name of the module, the rule will be compromised.

As will it be when the user changes item names... Of course, this is expected!

[2017-01-19T08:21:12Z | kaikreuzer | comment]
@danchom My PR #2850 is meant to provide a solution for the "simple rule editor" as discussed in https://github.com/eclipse/smarthome/issues/2763#issuecomment-272826754 and I think this addresses it nicely.

Your ideas regarding script actions with defined inputs is something that would only be relevant for a (not yet existing) expert rule editor. Ok for me to discuss what makes sense there , but I think it should be an independent discussion and not block #2850.

[2017-01-19T09:21:55Z | danchom | comment]
@Kai, I'm not blocking #2850, I just share our experience and how we implemented these module types. I'm ok the current PR to be merged.
@sjka 
>Why do you think it's convenient to have a fixed number of inputs

It's not convenient to have a fixed number and I'll open discussion to invent a way to define them dynamically (in time of rule creation)  
>and force the user to wire them in an additional step

This is normal way to exchange dynamic data between modules. Through the connections the user define (shows) source input data. At the moment you don't have opportunity to see your scriptCondition which item it checks.  
Also with the inputs you have opportunity to write scripts which other users can use in their rules. For example: The script: input1 + input2 + input3 + input4 + input5 will sum data of connected inputs and this script can be used independent of the state of the system and can be used in different usecase.
>Of course, this is what I would expect. What kind of useful input should come module wich did not trigger the rule?

There are different type of outputs. For example ItemTriggers.newState is example of stateful output, The timestamp of the TimerTrigger is stateless output. Why we need a stateful outputs?  For example if you want to create a rule which has to be executed when two items are ON, and do this with two comparator conditions (yes can do this ItemStateCondition but this is just an example and it only compare item states, it can't do some other complicated logic base on the state o fitems). Unfortunately this can't work because only one (the changed one) of comparators can be evaluated, the other won't receive input and logic and may be failed.
>As will it be when the user changes item names...

As Kai said the "advanced user" will write the script (script programmer), the user of home system, can decide to change a name of trigger of rule in his home and will brake the logic of script programmer. I think this is a real use case.

title: SMARTHOME/3746
body: The scheduling operations schedules few jobs and executes 2 specific jobs immediately. These two jobs are executed in a different thread to prevent blocking the thread that spawns it. In addition, during handler initialize, channel linking and unlinking, we reschedule the jobs. And every time, before we reschedule the jobs, we remove the jobs from the ESH Core scheduler that are associated with the current thing. As the jobs that execute immediately are handled by different threads, it is sometime noticed that while rescheduling, removal of jobs did occur after the jobs got rescheduled. This created unexpected issues in ESH Core scheduler. In this PR, we have rendered the asynchronous operations of executing immediate jobs in different threads to synchronous execution so that we can make sure the removal always happens before rescheduling. Another note is that previously we required `equals` and `hashcode` to be overriden by `AbstractJob` but currently it is not used anymore. These `equals` and `hashcode` affected normal executions of scheduled jobs as well. Hence, the methods have been removed.

[2019-02-07T08:49:55Z | Thomseeen | comment] Using the ESP-MQTT_FOR_IDF_3.1 release I still get that error on publishing data with over 16kB while having `CONFIG_USE_ONLY_LWIP_SELECT` set to `true`. Having lwip debug enabled my log looks like this when i try to publish a 17kB buffer: ``` tcp_write(pcb=0x3ffdf778, data=0x3ffe436c, len=5744, apiflags=3) tcp_write: queueing 6536:7972 tcp_write: queueing 7972:9408 tcp_write: queueing 9408:10844 tcp_write: queueing 10844:12280 tcp_output_segment: 6536:7972 tcp_output_segment: 7972:9408 tcp_output_segment: 9408:10844 tcp_output_segment: 10844:12280 +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+- tcp_input: flags -+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+ tcp_process: Connection RESET E (4691) MQTT_CLIENT: Error write data or timeout, written len = -1 E (4691) MQTT_CLIENT: Read error or end of stream E (4701) MQTT_CLIENT: Error to public data to topic=/topic/qos0, qos=0 ``` For some reason, looking at Wireshark, the first TCP-package gets followed by a response from my computer with a ACK and RST flag. Following that the other three packages shown above still reach my computer but get ignored. Edit: Seems likethere is an issue with the remaining length in the messages header. Sending a message with 16kB data and a topic length of 11B causes the header to be ``` 0x30, // Publish, no DUP, QoS 0, no Retain 0x8D, 0x7D, // remaining length of 16013B 0x00, 0x0B, // topic length 11B topic... ``` which works fine and is right according to MQTT 3.1. Sending a message with 17kB data and a topic length of 11B causes the header to be ``` 0x30, // Publish, no DUP, QoS 0, no Retain 0xF5, 0x84, // ... this is wrong. Beginning with the LSB (0x84) there is a continuation bit which would indicate a 3B long remaining length field. So the following 0x00 gets included into the remaining length field too. As a result the topic length field ix 0x0B and the first byte of the topic. That causes a wrong topic length and unreadable MQTT package. The right remaining length would be 3B (0xF5, 0x84, 0x01). 0x00, 0x0B, // topic length 11B topic... ``` [2019-03-28T21:15:00Z | david-cermak | comment] Hi all, Can we close this older issue? In embarc_osp project we get some hardware configuration from tcf file.

We generate CPU Frequency from macro definition core_config_clock_speed defined in tcf file, CPU Frequency = core_config_clock_speed*1000000. So check the core_config_clock_speed defined in your tcf file.

In freertos kernel example, we use TIMER1 for perf timer, so you need add TIMER1 support in tcf file.

title: EMBARC_OSP/74
body: # Issue Summary - **Type**: *Bug* - **Category**: *BSP* - **Release Version**: Specified version such as 2016.05 or All -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Bug ## Development Environment - **HOST OS**: Windows 10, 64bit - **TOOLCHAIN**: MWDT L-2017.06 - **BOARD**: EMSK 2.3 - **ARC CORE**: Any ## Bug Description FPU and DSP registers are not saved during handling of interrupts and exceptions, This may lead to undefined behavior. For my case: I have a thread that has a division operation, and there is a **vKernelTick** which is the ISR of tick timer of freertos port. This interrupt has also a division operation in calling of **board_timer_update**. **MW** is optimizing the local variables in case of division and use the **accl** and **acch** registers, so if the tick interrupt happens after performing the division operation and before using **accl** or **acch** register, there will be a corrupted values in those registers when returning from the ISR where an exception happened and the arc_reset is called. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Enhancement Adding the following code to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE and EXCEPTION_PROLOGUE at **arc_asm_common.h** ``` #if ARC_FEATURE_FPU_DSP_CONTEXT SAVE_R58_R59 SAVE_FPU_REGS SAVE_DSP_REGS #endif ``` and the following to INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE and EXCEPTION_EPILOGUE ``` #if ARC_FEATURE_FPU_DSP_CONTEXT RESTORE_DSP_REGS RESTORE_FPU_REGS RESTORE_R58_R59 #endif ``` same as SAVE_CALLEE_REGS and RESTORE_CALLEE_REGS.

[2019-03-14T08:02:10Z | vonhust | comment]
If interrupt handlers will use DSP/FPU (which is not recommended as these operations are time consuming), these registers should be pushed and popped

at the entry and exit of interrupts, i.e, move  the pop/push from SAVE_CALLEE_REGS/RESTORE_CALLEE_REGS to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE/ INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE.

The hardware will not push&pop these regs automatically (same for ARM).

So this is not a bug, but a choice.

[2019-04-02T15:07:34Z | mfarag13 | comment]
Hi @vonhust ,
DSP Operation (Division) is already used in an interrupt **vKernelTick**  at freertos port for ARC in function **board_timer_update**.
In this case freertos port should be updated. or we can add push/pop to INTERRUPT_PROLOGUE/ INTERRUPT_EPILOGUE.

This problem can be identified by looking at the `5750` key, this has a value of `2` when identified as a lamp and `0` when identified as a remote.

While figuring this out @ggravlingen and @lwis made a fix. That fix is now only worth something as a fallback for when this issue appears again.

The IKEA app identifies devices differently than Pytradfri does. IKEA doesn't seem to rely on the value of `5750` at all or on `3311` being present. Instead, the app probably looks at the presence of any lamp values (ex: Lamp state, dimmer value etc.). A curious choice when `5750` exists.

We can automate the detection of this issue, that might be a good addition to the examples or wiki.

title: HOMIE-ESP8266/242
body: I'm using the https://www.olimex.com/Products/IoT/ESP8266-EVB-BAT-BOX/open-source-hardware esp8266 with the current development homie firmware and the sketch that is shown at the end. The sketch runs fine for a couple of hours or days respectively, and then suddenly starts to resetting itself every 15 seconds or so. I did observe that on two different devices. I couldn't get serial output until now that would give more information on the cause of reset (hope to get to that when it happens again). From what I found so far on the internet, it all points to a watchdog timer issue. Did anybody have a similar experience? I had a similar sketch running with the stable 1.5 homie release and I didn't see experience any device resets. For the 2.0 sketch, I changed to bring down the relay in the loopHandler because the following sequence didn't work in relayToggleHandler any more: ``` if (value == "1" && digitalRead(PIN_RELAY) == LOW) { digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, HIGH); delay(250); digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, LOW); } ``` The relay didn't go to HIGH and back to LOW (it stayed LOW), I suppose that is related to the asynchronious nature in homie 2.0? **Homie 2.0.0 sketch:** ``` /* * Olimex esp8266 development board ESP8266 EVB-BAT * Firmware for Homie 2.0.0 with basic push button functionality. * */ #include <Homie.h> const int PIN_RELAY = 5; const int PIN_BUTTON = 0; unsigned long relayLastOn = 0; HomieNode relayNode("relay", "relay"); bool relayToggleHandler(HomieRange range, String value) { if (value == "1" && digitalRead(PIN_RELAY) == LOW) { digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, HIGH); relayNode.setProperty("on").send("true"); relayNode.setProperty("toggle").send("1"); relayLastOn = millis(); Serial << "Relay was toggled." << endl; } else { return false; } return true; } void loopHandler() { // bring the relay down to LOW after 250 ms, delay should not be called in any loop function if ( digitalRead(PIN_RELAY) == HIGH ) { unsigned long currentMillis = millis(); if ( (unsigned long)(currentMillis - relayLastOn) >= 250) { digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, LOW); relayNode.setProperty("on").send("false"); relayLastOn = currentMillis; } } } void setup() { Serial.begin(115200); Serial << endl << endl; // setup relay and button PIN pinMode(PIN_BUTTON, INPUT); pinMode(PIN_RELAY, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(PIN_RELAY, LOW); // Homie settings Homie_setFirmware("olimex-esp8266", "1.0.0"); //Homie.disableLedFeedback(); // reset device when pressing pin button for 5 sec (default) Homie.setResetTrigger(PIN_BUTTON, LOW, 5000); // relay only exposes a toggle property that // Use devices/dev-id/relay/toggle -> 1 to observe the relay // Use devices/dev-id/relay/toggle/set <- 1 to trigger the relay relayNode.advertise("toggle").settable(relayToggleHandler); relayNode.advertise("on"); Homie.setLoopFunction(loopHandler); Homie.setup(); } void loop() { Homie.loop(); } ```

body: Having an issue with Homie v2.0.0 MQTT $localip it gets truncated in the last symbol when published in MQTT: e.g. instead of "192.168.1.128" it gets "192.168.1.12", tested this on two nodes but with the same results.
comments:
[2017-02-28T11:13:59Z | bertmelis | comment]
try changing the file BootNormal.cpp on line 193:

```C++
snprintf(localIpStr, MAX_IP_STRING_LENGTH - 1, "%d.%d.%d.%d", localIp[0], localIp[1], localIp[2], localIp[3]);
```
to
```C++
snprintf(localIpStr, MAX_IP_STRING_LENGTH + 1, "%d.%d.%d.%d", localIp[0], localIp[1], localIp[2], localIp[3]);

If it works, you should also changed it BootConfig.cpp. But if this fix works, I would think the bug is that the IP gets truncated by 2 characters.

title: HOMIE-ESP8266/575
body: As you all probably know already, the Esp32-OTA implementation is not working properly. There's a problem with the getSketchMD5 esp32 function which ends in a boot loop. This function works properly in other sketchs and if we move the MD5 calculation from where it is (begining of bootnormal.cpp) in the bootnormal::setup procedure, it works without any problems.
comments:
[2019-04-04T14:51:48Z | bertmelis | comment]
`ESP.getSketchMD5()` is called in the BootNormal constructor. I also suggest to move this into `BootNormal::setup()` for both ESP8266 and ESP32. It's always tricky to call functions/methods in constructors for global objects.

Further improvement is to call `Update.end()` in `onMqttConnected()`. An MQTT disconnect during OTA ends up in a stale OTA update. Restarting an update doesn't work because `Update.begin()` returns `false` as there is still an update running.

Fixed by #593 😉

[2014-06-08T17:19:36Z | deadprogram | comment]
@blalor thanks for helping isolate this. I know @zankich has mentioned this problem before, but this is a good example case. We'll work on it.

[2014-06-09T23:20:12Z | stewart | comment]
Looking into this more, it's actually _technically_ not a bug. What's happening is due to Node's event loop, by the time the event listeners are attached for the devices, the events have already been emitted, so we can't hook into them. The exception is for the last device, which emits the 'start' event on the same tick that the work block begins processing and sets up the handlers.

The devices are all going to be started by the time the work block begins running, so the device 'start' events are more or less worthless, and will be removed from both docs and code shortly.

[2018-02-20T21:55:36Z | ikalchev | comment]
What follows is a guess, but I am very confident this is exactly what happens:

## Background
When iOS connects to an Accessory, it doesn't close the connection (socket) - it keeps it alive and doesn't say when it leaves (makes sense, because phones move, go to sleep, etc.). It is the accessory's responsibility to "expect" a dead connection.

So using this keep-alive connection, the accessory can send an event, which is what happens when you call `set_value(value, should_notify=True)`. But because the connection could be stale, HAP-python sets a timeout of 3 seconds for the send and if it doesn't happen, it shuts down the connection. After the send the timeout is removed.

On the same connection, iOS can decide to make a HTTP request, such as "set this value to this accessory" and waits for a reply to that request.
## The problem
When I set the timeout to None (i.e. no timeout) instead of 3 seconds, the problem vanishes completely. So I think there is some race condition in which the timeout is not removed properly, which causes a timeout in the thread that makes the request reply. What is more, I think that even if you use the "working" solution of ElectronicLock I posted earlier, there is a chance that it will also timeout.

Thanks for focusing my attention on this - I will try to address this ASAP.

title: WTHERMOSTATBECA/37
body: I've had to power of/ on my thermostat a couple of times in the last 3 months as it has dropped off the network and never reconnects (MQTT messages stop working/ there is no assigned DHCP lease etc). I suspect my automated AP firmware update causes the wireless to disconnect, but the thermostat simply never reconnects and is the only IOT device (of about 30) that doesn't. No SoftAP etc, it's just offline. The thermostat itself works, in that the relay is triggered at target temperature and the target temperature can be adjusted. Not sure if it matters but I tend to run with webServer set to false. Is there any way to increase logging/ send serial logs to MQTT or another source? Has anyone else experience issues such as this?

title: NODEL/99
body: The toolkit Timer uses *firstDelay* and *interval* parameters to control the timer behaviour. If the timer is stopped and the delay is ever re-set using **setDelay** or **setDelayAndInterval** methods, only the *interval* part is respected when the timer is restarted. Note, that when the timer is in a running state, the methods correctly behave as expected (both are respected). Correct behaviour would be for both parameters to be respected whether in a running or stopped state, with *firstDelay* reset every time a **setDelay___** function is used.

[2017-08-08T20:06:56Z | SergioRius | comment]
If you see this as an issue, I would understand the problem as an architectural issue. The structure clearly started as something simple, node-sensor. But now we must do more complex things.
Well I think the classes should be modified to allow better hierarchical organisation and iteration.
NodeManager is the root container. Should include a collection of "Sensors" what already does. But it mixes sensors and child. Collection nodes should be accessed like this:

`nodeManager.get(sensor).get(child)`

At some point, you would also want to access and modify base class elements, like settings. Then you will need a differentiation like this:

`nodeManager.Settings.LoopDelay = value`

And then:

`nodeManager.Sensors.Add(SENSOR_EXAMPLE, myOption)`
`nodeManager.Sensors(x).setType(V_ONETYPE)`
`nodemanager.Sensors(x).Child(y).setSamples(5)`

And you also can have defaults and/or apply properties to all child or first child. This makes it coherent and expandable.

`nodemanager.Sensors(x).Child.First.setSamples(5)`
`nodemanager.Sensors(x).Child.All.setSamples(5)`
`nodemanager.Sensors(x).setSamples(5) //All could be default`
`ForEach s in nodeManager.Sensors {...`

title: DEVICE-OS/1283
body: Attempts to restore 0.6.0-style arduino compatibility as outlined by issue #1278 In a nutshell: - the default is 0.6.0 Arduino compatibility - let's call this partial compatibility. - applications and libraries include "Arduino.h" to define `ARDUINO` and bring in many more additional defines to complete the Arduino API. We'll call this full compatibility. ## Mixing libraries that require partial and full Arduino compatibility Libraries that require full Arduino compatibility may include Arduino.h in their library header file, while libraries that depend on partial compatibility (because they themselves define missing symbols) don't include Arduino.h. If a library requiring partial compatibility is included after one requiring full compatibility then the partial compatibility library may break, since Arduino symbols that it's not expecting will be defined. title: SMARTHOME/184
body: When using relative items in combination with a function, lets say a "changed_by()" or "last_update()" the relative item gets misinterpreted. Easiest way to solve I guess is to search for () and then interpret the dots differently. sh...changed_by() should look for the change of the item itself.. though having three consecutive points looks a bit weird ;)
comments:
[2016-12-31T10:29:24Z | msinn | comment]
Using relative addressing with internal attributes was not the initial usecase.

I am looking into it

[2017-01-02T15:09:55Z | msinn | comment]
@onkelandy From what I found out, your problem only exists, if you want to address a function for the item itself (eg..: 'sh...changed_by()') and direct ancestors, but not for referencing other items like 'sh..sister.changed_by()'.

Interpreting the dots in another way if parentheses are present gives a lot of other problems. The solution I found is the following: Inserting a reserved word 'self'. 

To reference the item itself you can use '.self' instead of '.'. So instead of writing 'sh...changed_by()' (which produces unexpected results), you could write 'sh..self.changed_by()'.

Or for referencing a function of the parent item, instead of writing 'sh....changed_by()' (which produces unexpected results), you can write 'sh...self.changed_by()'

What do you think about that solution?

[2017-01-02T15:21:55Z | onkelandy | comment]
Sounds like a fair solution.. Though I think the dots in general are very irritating especially when combined with sh.
Wouldnt a delimiter, something like sh.[.].changed_by() work and make it more readable?

[2017-01-02T15:29:00Z | msinn | comment]
I am not sure, if it would make things even more complex. There has been a discussion about escape-chars for relative addressing in the past, but without a good solution. But that discussion has not dealt with usage of internal attributes of an item.

[2017-01-02T15:38:58Z | msinn | comment]
It will take a couple of days for the modification to be included in the dev repository, because I am doing some renovation on the autotimer handling for items. Until then you could only use a workaround  with addressing using the parent item like:

```
current_item -> .
parent_item -> ..

sh...changed_by()                # is not working at the moment
sh...current_item.changed_by()   # workaround
```

[2017-01-02T15:42:09Z | onkelandy | comment]
thx! I've already changed the references to global ones but maybe it's useful for someone else.

[2017-01-21T15:29:27Z | msinn | comment]

title: SYNSE-SERVER/88
body: ## Description It seems like when a device does not have any data (e.g. the plugin SDK fails to read anything off of a configured device) we either: - get `"null"` back as the reading value in a valid 200 read response - get a 500 specifying that no readings are found The behavior here should be unified so we always expect the same thing for the same class of error. I'm not sure what conditions make it so that "null" is returned vs. a 500, so that will need to be investigated first. To recreate this, there can be a device configured in a plugin that doesn't physically exist, so the SDK can't read off of it. Then read that device off of Synse Server. I think that returning "null" (or the actual `null` type) should be fine, but I'd like to hear what others think -- does it seem like returning `null` is better, or returning a 500 error when there are no readings for a configured device. Note that this case of 'no readings' can occur when: - a device is configured but doesnt exist - a device is unplugged/unreachable - a device fails and can no longer be read from

[2018-03-12T21:13:33Z | timfallmk | comment]

Could we throw a 404 for not found/not reachable? If not present in the config, I'd like to see that as an error. Any failures in the process should be reported if categorizable, and if not then 500 as a last resort.

body: <!-- Thank you for reporting a possible bug in YodaRT. Please fill in as much of the template below as you can. Version: output of `getprop | grep ro.rokid.build.yodaos | awk '{ print $2 }'` Platform: output of `uname -a` Subsystem: if known, please specify the affected core module name If possible, please provide code that demonstrates the problem, keeping it as simple and free of external dependencies as you can. --> * **Version**: next * **Platform**: all * **Subsystem**: runtime <!-- Please provide more details below this comment. --> Here is the example to reproduce this problem: ```js rt.openUrl('yoda-app://telephony?from=+3678') ``` Then the `url.query` object should be: ```js { from: ' 3678' } ``` A possible solution should call `encodeURI` or `encodeURIComponent` before calling the parse function.
comments:
[2019-06-30T08:02:55Z | yorkie | comment]
Related source lines are: https://github.com/yodaos-project/yodart/blob/next/runtime/app-runtime.js#L257-L274.

[2019-06-30T11:25:30Z | legendecas | comment]
Character + would be parsed as white space in URL spec. All characters except A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ! ~ * ' ( ) must be escaped in URI components.

Ok, I see and closing this :)
